final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly narrowed the interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation is directionally more accurate than any broader claim that rollout controls cure the weakness, but it does not resolve the core compliance predicate. The admissible evidence still shows: aggregate readiness passed and rehearsal had no severity-one incidents; the rollout is limited and reversible but still includes the affected public benefits eligibility segment; that segment remains below target; the risk-acceptance draft is neither approved nor on point; and policy requires disclosure for material limitations affecting named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The distinction matters: a caveated certification theory could become supportable if there were admissible evidence that explicit pre-launch disclosure was actually completed, but there is no such evidence in this packet. Because the missing disclosure evidence is itself the unresolved compliance condition, this is not yet compliant_with_caveats on the present record. The Actor's business-cost framing and narrower wording do not substitute for proof that the required disclosure happened.
